name: Anisotropic Total Variation
definition: A regularization prior defined as the sum of absolute differences along the three principal axes (x, y, z) for each voxel. It is represented as $\tilde{g}(K\mathbf{x})$ where $\tilde{g}(\cdot)$ is the $l_1$ norm and $K=D$ is the forward difference matrix.
summary: Anisotropic Total Variation is a regularization prior that enforces piecewise constant solutions by summing absolute differences along principal axes, favoring axis-aligned edges over isotropic smoothing.
